\begin{circuitikz}[

  \node[op amp] (B) at (0,0) {};
  \node at (B.center) {\footnotesize A2};
  \draw (B.+) -- (-1.6,-0.3);
  \draw (-1.6,-0.3) to[V, l_=$V_{\mathrm{CM}}$, invert] (-1.6,-2.8) node[ground]{};
  \draw (B.-) -- (-3.0,0.3);
  \node[railnode] at (-3.0,0.3){};
  \node[nlab, above=3pt] at (-3.0,0.3){\texttt{WE}};
  \draw (-3.0,0.3) to[I, l_=$i_{\mathrm{we}}$] (-3.0,-2.8) node[ground]{};
  \draw (-3.0,0.3) -- (-4.6,0.3);

  \draw (-3.0,0.3) -- (-3.0,2.2);
  \draw (-3.0,2.2) -- (-2.3,2.2);

  \node[nlab, above=2pt] at (PB.north) {\texttt{IPRB\_F}};

  \draw (-1.2,2.2) to[R, l=$R_f$] (1.6,2.2);
  \draw (1.6,2.2) -- (1.6,0);
  \draw (B.out) -- (1.6,0);
  \node[railnode] at (1.6,0){};
  \node[nlab, below right] at (1.7,-0.05){\texttt{V\_OUT}};
  \draw (1.6,0) -- (3.0,0);

  }
  \caption[{Closed transimpedance loop, \texttt{TiaFbTB}.}]{The closed transimpedance loop, \texttt{TiaFbTB}, the only bench in this section that closes feedback around the electrode. \(R_f\) returns the output to the working electrode through the probe \texttt{IPRB\_F}, and \(i_{\mathrm{we}}\) is the swept test source; every closed-loop figure in Section~\ref{sss:tia-loop} comes from here. \textbf{The electrode is a bare \SI{1}{\micro\farad} to ground, not the Randles cell of Figure~\ref{fig:randles-cell}}, which is why the reported peaking is an upper bound. The probe is present but only an \texttt{ac} analysis was run, so the loop gain itself is not measured.}
